title: New Mexico Navajo Water Settlement Technical Corrections Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the House reported version is repeated here.)

New Mexico Navajo Water Settlement Technical Corrections Act

(Sec. 2) Amends the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 to expand the current authorization for the construction or rehabilitation and operation and maintenance of conjunctive use wells in the San Juan River Basin, Little Colorado River Basin, and Rio Grande Basin in New Mexico to include the planning and design of those wells.

Revises the percentages of funds authorized for the Navajo-Gallup Water Supply Project, conjunctive use wells, and San Juan River Irrigation Projects that may be made available for specified purposes by:

  • increasing from 2% to 4% the portion of funds that may be used for the survey, recovery, protection, preservation, and display of archaeological resources in the area of a Project facility or conjunctive use well; and
  • decreasing from 4% to 2% the portion of funds that may be used for purchasing land and constructing and maintaining facilities to mitigate the loss of, and improve conditions for the propagation of, fish and wildlife.

Makes technical corrections.

summary.headline: This law makes technical fixes to a 2009 New Mexico water settlement law, mainly expanding well planning and shifting how some project funds can be spent.
summary.what_it_does: It changes the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 so that the authorized work on conjunctive use wells in three New Mexico river basins now includes planning and design, not just construction, rehabilitation, and operation. It raises from 2% to 4% the share of project funds that can go toward surveying, protecting, and displaying archaeological resources near project facilities or wells. It lowers from 4% to 2% the share that can go toward buying land and building facilities for fish and wildlife. It also makes other technical corrections.

who_it_affects.group: Navajo Nation communities and residents in northwestern New Mexico
who_it_affects.how: They are covered by the Navajo-Gallup water supply and related water projects that this change adjusts.

who_it_affects.group: Water users in the San Juan, Little Colorado, and Rio Grande basins in New Mexico
who_it_affects.how: Conjunctive use wells in these basins can now be funded for planning and design as well as construction and operation.

who_it_affects.group: Archaeologists and historic preservation organizations working near project sites
who_it_affects.how: More project funding can be used for surveying and protecting archaeological resources near project facilities.

who_it_affects.group: Fish and wildlife conservation groups and land managers in the project areas
who_it_affects.how: The share of project funds available for land purchases and wildlife mitigation facilities is reduced.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on September 30, 2015, and the changes took effect on that date.
